suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-20 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited systematic review of observational studies ascertained the malignant transformation rate of oral leukoplakia and its risk factors, reporting that a meaningful proportion of oral leukoplakias progress to oral squamous cell carcinoma. Require a biopsy-documented oral leukoplakia and separately established oral squamous cell carcinoma with compatible chronology; the cited systematic review of observational studies reported that a meaningful proportion of oral leukoplakias undergo malignant transformation to oral squamous cell carcinoma, without establishing that any individual's cancer arose from the leukoplakic lesion. Preserve tobacco use, alcohol use, other potentially malignant disorders (erythroplakia, oral submucous fibrosis), HPV infection, immunocompromise, and other oral-cancer risk factors as competing explanations. Do not infer cancer from clinical appearance or from dysplasia alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that oral leukoplakia caused an individual's oral cancer. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
